comments_text: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (71.43%) to (WR)3-NH2 W=R: 50%. Activity: Active against B. subtilis 168 (MIC 2 ug/ml), S. aureus SG511 or Mu50 VISA or ATCC43300 MRSA (MIC 8-16 ug/ml), S. aureus COL/MRSA (MIC 96 ug/ml), E. coli DSM30083 (MIC 32 ug/ml), E-coli W3110 (MIC >64 ug/ml) A. baumannii DSM30007 (MIC 32 ug/ml), P-aeruginosa PAO1 (MIC >64 ug/ml) ( Wenzel et al., 2016). MOA:bacteria:E. coli: act on membranes. proteomic study revealed 134 proteins were differentially expressed, leading to the upregulation of the envelope stress induced protein and down-regulation of the mechano-sensitive channel MscL and so on ( Fränzel et al., 2012). Also cause selective ion release from B. subtitlis ( Wenzel et al., 2015). Resistance development:no:bacteria:B. subtilis: when treated at 4xMIC, no resistant colonies of B. subtilis were observed after 24 and 48 h (spontaneous resistance). In vitro Toxicity: caused shrinkage of murine RBC at 250 ug/ml (14% lysis) and cell damage at 500 ug/ml (23% lysis): low hemo.lytic. Not significantly cytotoxic against human liver carcinoma, colon adenocarcinoma, and breast cancer cell lines. Antimicrobial robustness: serum-sensitive: 50% activity is lost in the presence of undiluted bovin serum. Peptide conjugate:carbohydrate-binding module/protein (CBM): The CBM3-MP196-modified materials displayed antibacterial activity against E. coli, P. aeruginosa and S. aureus significantly higher than that of materials prepared by physical adsorption of MP196.
